The computation lives in src/tools/bunker_shot_gui/model.py, which imports no GUI toolkit and is the layer a React port would consume; the v1 API route (#9545) serves a bounded nominal solve, the A/B comparison with the model's carry-objective standing (no predictive winner on an unqualified objective, #9239) and digest verification of saved records from it. The web page (/tools/bunker-workbench, #9545 slice 3) runs the evaluate and compare solves through the job routes (slice 5): two designs (loft, marketed bounce, sole width; blank keeps the grind preset), an exploratory carry objective, and per result the tier, verdict, in-frame stamp, sand-property sources and digest; the comparison shows the objective standing and names a winner only on a predictive standing, otherwise an exploratory leader (#9239). The same two solves also run as bounded, cancellable jobs (/v1/jobs/evaluate, /v1/jobs/compare, then poll /v1/jobs/{job_id} for per-shot progress or POST .../cancel; slice 4) on the shared API TaskManager: at most two workers, a cancelled job stops before its next shot and never gains a result, and a completed result names its job id and input digest so a stale answer is recognisable. The page (slice 5) submits each solve as a job, polls its status on a bounded backed-off schedule (250 ms doubling to 2 s, giving up after three failed reads in a row) that stops on a terminal state, a cancel or unmount, shows a labelled progress bar of the per-shot progress with a keyboard-reachable Cancel button, shows failed and cancelled jobs as such, and discards as stale any result whose job id, kind or input digest does not match the current submission. Workbench figures export through src/tools/bunker_shot_gui/export.py (slice 8): a PNG whose iTXt header carries the view, verdict status, tier, in-frame stamp words, sources and an optional v1 record digest, sealed by a SHA-256 over the header and the decoded pixels; export_figure refuses a figure that does not draw the stamp it claims, and read_export refuses an unstamped, edited, unknown-schema or predictive-claiming file. The PyQt window has no Export action yet. It stays a gap: no sand/swing inputs, no /v1/verify save-and-reload, no visualizations, and no rendered acceptance evidence. Under Tauri the tile still opens the PyQt window; the page is the browser fallback. The visualization suite (epic #8699) keeps that split: shot3d.py and traces.py compute, render3d.py and render_traces.py draw headlessly through matplotlib, and viewport_widgets.py only wires them to a canvas. A React port would consume shot3d.viewport_payload, which is the backend-neutral ADR-0027 ViewportOverlayPayload and carries the envelope status and fidelity tier in its metadata so any renderer can stamp its own frames. The F1 sand cut (#8710, #8711) keeps the same split and adds one constraint a port must honour: the field carries its fidelity tier and validity status as data covered by a SHA-256 over the provenance and the arrays together, so any client that renders a field must read the standing out of the file rather than out of its filename, and must refuse a field whose digest does not match.
